subject: AP authorization for one-time wire to avoid virtual-card fee
messages:
From: Alyssa Ramos <alyssa@luminahealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lumina AP <ap@luminahealth.com>
Date: 2028-09-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Lumina invoice 2028-09-03 / payment method

Hi Irene / Ben,

Thanks — we received invoice INV-4821 for Redwood services dated Sep 3. Our AP team is set up to pay via virtual card on the platform by default. That route will post within 5 business days but includes a 2% processing fee.

Before we proceed, finance asked whether Redwood can accept a one-time ACH or bank wire for this invoice to avoid the fee (they prefer wire for larger vendors). If so, could you confirm:

- Bank name & account details (or a vendor portal link)
- Any required vendor forms / tax docs you need from us
- Preferred remittance note (PO or invoice number to include)

Attached is a screenshot of the AP portal showing the payment options for reference. If virtual card is the only option, please let us know and we’ll route accordingly.

Cheers,
Alyssa Ramos
Vendor Payments — Lumina Health
alyssa@luminahealth.com

Attachment: Lumina_AP_Portal_Screenshot.pdf (image/pdf)

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Ramos <alyssa@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-09-11T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumina invoice 2028-09-03 / payment method

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the heads up.

We can accept a one-time wire or ACH for INV-4821. For ACH, we typically ask for a remittance reference with invoice number + entity name (Redwood Inference LLC) so reconciliation is smooth. For wire, please include the invoice number and the billing entity.

Bank details (wire + ACH):
- Bank: First Harbor Bank
- Account name: Redwood Inference LLC
- Routing (ACH): 021000021
- Account number: ****1234 (I’ll send full account via secure channel/DocuSign once you confirm wire)

Vendor forms: we need a completed W-9 (attached) and your AP’s billing contact. If Lumina prefers, we can open a short vendor onboarding task in our portal and share a secure bank info upload link (DocuSign).

If you confirm wire/ACH, I’ll loop in Ben for the remittance tag and ask finance to approve a one-time wire exception to avoid the card fee. If you choose virtual card, we’ll accept that too — just let me know which path you want.

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
irene@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Redwood_Vendor_W9.pdf (pdf)

From: Alyssa Ramos <alyssa@luminahealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-09-11T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumina invoice 2028-09-03 / payment method

Irene — thanks, that helps. Our AP policy defaults to virtual card because it automates reconciliation for their ERP; getting a wire requires a manager sign-off and an internal PO. They can do the wire for this invoice but asked whether Redwood can accept the wire confirmation email as the remittance (they usually require the invoice number to be in the wire description).

Action items from our side:
- We can provide a scanned PO by EOD if that speeds approvals.
- Lumina AP will sign off on the wire if you confirm the bank details over DocuSign (security team requirement).

I’ll collect the PO and loop in AP. Please send the secure bank info link and we’ll route the wire (to avoid the 2% card fee).

—Alyssa

Ben / Priyom — forwarding Lumina’s response. They can provide a PO and Lumina AP will sign off if we provide the bank details via DocuSign. Their default is virtual card (2% fee).

Request: can finance approve a one-time wire for INV-4821 to avoid the fee? This is a clean customer, non-disputed invoice, invoice total $63,400. If you approve, I’ll initiate the DocuSign bank-info exchange and confirm remittance tag.

If we prefer to take the card, we should accept the fee and confirm final posted date (5 business days).

Proposed next step: Priyom — quick sign-off (yes/no) on waiver for wire exception so I can move this to DocuSign and get the PO.

Thanks,
Irene
